name: Roberto Baggio
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1993 Ballon d'Or and FIFA World Player of the Year at age 26, capping a rise from Serie C1 debut at 16 to Juventus stardom and UEFA Cup victory.
early_history_summary: Baggio began his youth career at Caldogno at age 9, was acquired by Vicenza's youth team at 13, and made his professional debut in Serie C1 at 16 in 1983. He moved to Fiorentina in 1985 for £1.5M, debuted in Serie A at 19, and transferred to Juventus in 1990 for a world record fee. By 1993 he had won the UEFA Cup with Juventus and was named both Ballon d'Or and FIFA World Player of the Year.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Baggio grew up in Caldogno, a small town in northern Italy; no evidence of unusual family financial status or domain connections found.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Italian football pipeline, early professional debut, Serie A ecosystem, physical talent
evidence_summary: Baggio was scouted at age 9, scored 45 goals in 26 matches at age 11, and was acquired by Vicenza at 13. He debuted professionally at 16 in Serie C1 and reached Serie A by 19 with Fiorentina. His transfer to Juventus in 1990 for a world record fee and subsequent 1993 Ballon d'Or/FIFA World Player of the Year at age 26 represent a clear trajectory of early specialization within Italy's elite football pipeline. No family background advantages were documented in reviewed sources, but the Italian football scouting and development system provided a clear elite performance pipeline.

name: Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan
milestone_by_age_26: Became head of the family qawwali party in 1971 at age 22-23, with major hits in Pakistan including 'Ni Main Jana Jogi De Naal' composed and first performed that year, and was an established Radio Pakistan performer by his late teens.
early_history_summary: Born into a 600-year qawwali family tradition, Khan joined his father's qawwali party as a tabla player in his youth. After his father's death in 1964, he became lead singer at 16 alongside his uncle. His first public performance as leader was broadcast on Radio Pakistan in March 1965. After his uncle's death in 1971, he became head of the family qawwali party and composed early major hits.
family_context_summary: Khan was born into a Punjabi Muslim family with an unbroken tradition of performing qawwali for approximately 600 years. His father, Fateh Ali Khan, was a distinguished musicologist, vocalist, instrumentalist, and qawwal. The family lived modestly in a rented flat in Lyallpur (Faisalabad).
parent_family_domain_summary: Khan's father was a celebrated qawwali singer and musicologist who initially resisted Nusrat entering the profession due to low social status of qawwals, but eventually trained him. His uncle Mubarak Ali Khan completed his training after his father's death in 1964.
primary_early_advantage_tags: 600-year qawwali family tradition, father as mentor, Radio Pakistan platform, uncle's training, early public performance
evidence_summary: Khan was born into a 600-year family tradition of qawwali performance. His father Fateh Ali Khan was a renowned musicologist and qawwal who trained him from childhood, initially as a tabla player. After his father's death in 1964, his uncle Mubarak Ali Khan completed his training. Khan gave his first public performance as leader on Radio Pakistan in March 1965 at age 16, and became head of the family qawwali party in 1971 at age 22-23, composing major hits. The family lived modestly, but the inherited musical tradition and direct mentorship from father and uncle provided extraordinary domain depth.

name: Filippo Inzaghi
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Capocannoniere (Serie A top scorer) with 24 goals for Atalanta in the 1996-97 season at age 23, and was named Serie A Young Footballer of the Year, before transferring to Juventus and winning the Scudetto.
early_history_summary: Inzaghi began his youth career at San Nicolò (1982-85) and Piacenza (1985-91). He turned professional with Piacenza in 1991, had loan spells at AlbinoLeffe and Verona, then helped Piacenza win Serie B in 1994-95. After a brief stint at Parma, he moved to Atalanta in 1996 where he became Serie A top scorer at 23, earning a transfer to Juventus in 1997.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Inzaghi was born in Piacenza, Italy, and his younger brother Simone Inzaghi also became a professional footballer, suggesting a football-oriented family environment.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources, though his brother Simone also became a professional footballer, suggesting some family exposure to the sport.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Italian football pipeline, Piacenza youth academy, Serie A ecosystem, sibling footballer
evidence_summary: Inzaghi progressed through Italian youth football at San Nicolò and Piacenza, turning professional at 18. After loan spells in lower divisions, he broke through at Atalanta in 1996-97, becoming Serie A top scorer at 23 with 24 goals and winning Young Footballer of the Year. This earned him a transfer to Juventus where he won the Scudetto. His brother Simone also became a professional footballer, suggesting a football-oriented family, but no specific family advantages were documented. The Italian football pipeline provided the key elite performance pathway.

name: Nigel Mansell

name: Giorgio Moroder

name: Dan Shechtman
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Shechtman earned his B.Sc. in Mechanical Engineering from Technion in 1966 (age 25) and was working on his M.Sc. by 26. His discovery of quasicrystals came at age 41 in 1982, and the Nobel Prize in Chemistry at age 70 in 2011.

name: Felice Gimondi
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1965 Tour de France at age 22 in his first year as a professional cyclist, and went on to win the Giro d'Italia (1967) and Vuelta a España (1968) by age 25-26, becoming the second cyclist to win all three Grand Tours.
early_history_summary: Gimondi grew up in Sedrina, Bergamo, son of a transport manager and post mistress. He rode the 1964 Olympics and won the Tour de l'Avenir (amateur stage race) that year. Signed as a professional by Salvarani in 1965, he was a last-minute addition to their Tour de France team and won the overall title in his rookie pro season at age 22.
primary_leverage_engine: Physical talent and early specialization in cycling
family_context_summary: Gimondi was the son of a transport manager and a post mistress in Sedrina, Bergamo. He frequently took his mother's post bicycle and helped deliver mail on it, providing early cycling exposure. No evidence of unusual financial status found.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. His mother's post bicycle provided early riding exposure, but no family cycling background was documented.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Italian cycling tradition, Salvarani team, Tour de l'Avenir win, early pro debut, mother's post bicycle
evidence_summary: Gimondi grew up in Bergamo, a cycling-rich region of Italy, and used his mother's post bicycle for early riding. He won the Tour de l'Avenir in 1964 (amateur) and was signed by Salvarani in 1965. As a last-minute Tour de France replacement, he won the overall title at 22 in his first professional year, an extraordinary achievement. He then won the Giro d'Italia (1967) and Vuelta a España (1968) by 25-26. No significant family advantages were documented beyond access to a bicycle, but the Italian cycling ecosystem and Salvarani team provided an elite performance pipeline.

name: Carlos Pace

name: Carlos Alberto Torres
milestone_by_age_26: Captained Brazil to victory in the 1970 FIFA World Cup at age 25-26, scoring the iconic fourth goal in the final against Italy, widely considered one of the greatest goals in World Cup history.
early_history_summary: Carlos Alberto began playing as a junior at Fluminense at age 15, established himself in the first team by 18, and was drafted into the Brazilian national squad before 20. He debuted for Brazil in 1964 marking Bobby Charlton. After leading Fluminense to the Carioca championship in 1965, he transferred to Santos in 1966 at age 22 for a record Brazilian fee, playing alongside Pelé. He captained Brazil to the 1970 World Cup title.
family_context_summary: Carlos Alberto came from a family with three brothers who all played football. He was spotted by Fluminense coaches as a youth. No evidence of unusual financial status was found in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. His brothers also played football, suggesting a football-oriented family environment, but no specific parental domain expertise was documented.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Brazilian football pipeline, Fluminense youth system, Santos with Pelé, 1970 World Cup, early national team debut
evidence_summary: Carlos Alberto was spotted by Fluminense coaches at 15 and joined their youth system, training with professionals and receiving professional coaching. By 18 he was in the Fluminense first team, and by 19-20 he was capped for Brazil. He transferred to Santos in 1966 at 22 for a record fee, playing alongside Pelé. At 25-26 he captained Brazil to the 1970 World Cup victory. The Brazilian football apprentice system, where juniors trained with professionals and were drafted in as cover, provided a direct elite performance pipeline. His brothers also played football, suggesting a football-oriented family, but no specific financial or domain advantages were documented.

name: Shakira
milestone_by_age_26: Released breakthrough album Pies Descalzos (1995) at age 18, which sold over 5 million copies and established her across Latin America; followed by Dónde Están los Ladrones? (1998) and Laundry Service (2001) which sold 13M+ copies, making her a global superstar by age 24.
early_history_summary: Shakira wrote her first poem at 4 and first song at 8. She was signed by Sony Music Colombia at 13 after impressing executives at an audition. Her debut album Magia was released at 14 (1991) but sold poorly. After a second failed album, she broke through with Pies Descalzos in 1995 at 18, which spawned multiple hit singles across Latin America. By 2001, Laundry Service made her a global crossover star.
family_context_summary: Shakira was born to William Mebarak Chadid and Nidia Ripoll Torrado in Barranquilla, Colombia. Her father was a jeweler who went bankrupt when she was 8, after which the family lost their cars and furniture. She has eight older half-siblings from her father's previous marriage. The family lived in reasonably comfortable conditions before the bankruptcy.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Her father was a jeweler, not connected to the music industry. No parental music domain expertise was documented.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Early songwriting, Sony Music Colombia signing, Latin pop wave, family bankruptcy, prodigy-level talent
evidence_summary: Shakira demonstrated extraordinary early talent, writing poetry at 4 and songs at 8, and belly dancing from age 4 after hearing Arabic music at a restaurant. A local theater producer convinced Sony Music Colombia to audition her at 13, leading to a three-album deal. After two commercial failures, she asserted creative control and broke through with Pies Descalzos at 18, selling 5M+ copies. Her father's bankruptcy at her age 8 created financial adversity, but also seemed to catalyze her drive. By 24, Laundry Service sold 13M+ copies globally. No family music connections or financial advantages were documented; her rise was largely self-created through prodigy-level talent and persistence.

name: Jim Morrison
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded The Doors in 1965 at age 21-22, released the self-titled debut album in January 1967 at 23, and scored a #1 US hit single with 'Light My Fire' in July 1967, becoming one of the most iconic frontmen in rock history by his mid-20s.
early_history_summary: Morrison grew up in a military family, attended Florida State University, then transferred to UCLA's film program around 1964-65. He met Ray Manzarek in Venice, California in 1965 and founded The Doors. After two years of obscurity playing Sunset Strip clubs, they signed with Elektra Records in 1966 and released their debut album in January 1967, with 'Light My Fire' reaching #1 by July 1967.
family_context_summary: Morrison was the son of Admiral George Stephen Morrison, a career U.S. Navy officer who commanded U.S. naval forces during the Gulf of Tonkin incident in 1964. This provided a middle-class military family upbringing but also a rebellious counterpoint for Morrison. He had an IQ of 149, tested in the top 0.1%.
parent_family_domain_summary: His father was a U.S. Navy admiral, providing no direct music industry connections. The military family background may have contributed to Morrison's rebellious artistic persona, but no parental domain advantage in music was documented.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Los Angeles Sunset Strip, 1960s counterculture wave, Ray Manzarek partnership, UCLA film school, military family rebellion
evidence_summary: Morrison grew up in a Navy family (father was an admiral) and attended UCLA's film program, where he absorbed surrealist and literary influences. He met keyboardist Ray Manzarek in Venice, California in 1965 and founded The Doors. The Los Angeles Sunset Strip club scene of 1965-66 provided a frontier geography for the emerging counterculture rock movement. After signing with Elektra Records in 1966, their debut album (January 1967) and 'Light My Fire' (#1 July 1967) made Morrison an icon at 23. The complementary partnership with Manzarek, Krieger, and Densmore was critical. Morrison's military family background provided financial stability but also fueled his rebellious persona. His IQ of 149 suggests high cognitive ability.
